plan: My private value is $23. In a first-price sealed bid auction with payment at third-highest bid, I want to bid strategically. Since my value is moderate, I'll bid somewhat below my true value to maximize potential profit. A bid around $20 leaves room for potential gain if others bid higher. I'll aim to win only if the price is sufficiently below my true value, protecting against overpaying.

My private value is $18. To maximize profit, I want to bid strategically close to my value. Since the winning bid pays the third-highest bid, I should bid slightly above my value to increase chances of winning, but not so high that I risk losing money. Given the $0-$49 range and one-shot nature, I'll bid around $20 - just above my value to potentially capture profit if others bid lower, but not overcommit.

My private value is $25. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. Since the third-highest bid determines my payment, bidding $25 ensures I maximize potential profit if I win. With values drawn randomly between $0-$49, other bidders might have values above or below mine. I'll bid close to my true value to balance winning probability and potential profit.
